primitives.name: Playcalling Tendencies
primitives.verbatim_quote: @sfdata9ers — "Week 1 Offensive Playcalling Tendencies" table (Motion/Screen/Play Action/No Huddle/RPO percentages per team, data credited to @FTNFantasy); "Kickoff Coverage: Average Opponent Drive Start" chart; "Josh Allen Career EPA/Play" career heatmap.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{motion}': 'dimensionless probability of motion plays', 'p_{screen}': 'dimensionless probability of screen plays', 'p_{action}': 'dimensionless probability of play-action', 'p_{huddle}': 'dimensionless probability of no-huddle', 'p_{rpo}': 'dimensionless probability of RPO'}
primitives.assumptions: Plays are independently sampled from a categorical distribution with fixed probabilities per team and week.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Categorical frequency sampling with minimum volume threshold of 100 plays per team per week.

primitives.name: Offensive Matchup Grades
primitives.verbatim_quote: @ThunderDanDFS (Thunder Dan Palyo, RotoBaller) — "Week 2 Offensive Matchup Grades" tables with columns Team / Implied Total / Opponent / Passing Matchup grade / Rushing Matchup grade, stated to use 2026-season data only; plus his RB rushing matchup grades that incorporate O-line data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'g_{pass}': 'dimensionless passing matchup grade', 'g_{rush}': 'dimensionless rushing matchup grade', 't_{implied}': 'points, implied total from betting markets'}
primitives.assumptions: Matchup grades are normalized scores based on opponent defensive strength and player-specific performance history.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Normalized score range [0,100] with peer group adjustment for positional strength.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's player-level expected value model using weighted regression on opponent defense stats.
layer2.telemetry: Observed fantasy point projections vs actual outcomes.

primitives.name: Game Facet Attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: @SamHoppen — "How the game was won" charts breaking Win Probability Added and Total EPA into 10 game facets (Pass Off, Run Off, Pass Def, Run Def, Takeaways, Giveaways, Off Pen, Def Pen, Special Teams, Other), data credited to nflfastR.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'wpa_{facet}': 'dimensionless WPA contribution per facet', 'epa_{facet}': 'expected points added per facet'}
primitives.assumptions: Each facet contributes independently to overall game outcome with additive EPA/WPA components.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Discrete time-series decomposition of game events into 10 orthogonal categories.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's game-state evolution kernel via time-weighted EPA contributions per facet.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative EPA/WPA per game facet over time.

The three core primitives—playcalling tendencies, matchup grades, and game facet attribution—are mathematically unified through probabilistic event spaces defined by categorical play types, normalized scoring functions, and time-series decompositions. Each primitive operates within a shared domain of discrete NFL actions, where inputs are mapped to scalar outputs via regression or classification kernels. Playcalling tendencies form a categorical distribution over play types, which can be modeled as a multinomial process with fixed parameters per team. Matchup grades are derived from normalized regressions against opponent defensive profiles, forming a continuous score space. Game facets represent a partitioning of the game timeline into orthogonal components, enabling additive decomposition of win probability and expected points. These primitives exhibit dualities in their construction: one rooted in empirical frequency (tendencies), another in comparative performance (grades), and a third in temporal segmentation (facets). Failure modes include insufficient sample size in early seasons, overfitting to specific matchups, and misalignment between game state and attribution models. The epistemic structure supports replication via public data sources such as nflfastR, PFF, and FTN Fantasy, with minimal proprietary elements.
